query: How can businesses improve Yelp user satisfaction?

per_column.name: service_attentiveness
per_column.rationale: Service attentiveness is a controllable operational lever a business can set by training and staffing; plausibly affects user satisfaction.

per_column.name: staff_communication_quality
per_column.rationale: Staff communication quality is an intervenable practice a business can improve through training and policy; a valid what-if lever on satisfaction.

per_column.name: food_taste_execution
per_column.rationale: Food taste/execution is settable via recipes, ingredients, and kitchen practices; an intervenable driver of satisfaction.

per_column.name: ambiance_comfort
per_column.rationale: Ambiance/comfort is a configurable property of the venue (seating, decor, layout) that a business can change; intervenable lever affecting satisfaction.

judge.rationale: The query is explicitly interventional ('How can businesses improve user satisfaction?'), and all four added columns are intervenable levers a business could actually set or change (service, communication, food, ambiance), so requirement (a) is satisfied. However, the columns are entirely a set of candidate treatments/drivers. Requirement (b) is NOT met: there is not a single confounder -- no common cause of both a given treatment and satisfaction (e.g., price tier, restaurant category/cuisine, location/neighborhood affluence, reviewer strictness, time period). Without any adjustment variables, the counterfactual effect of any lever cannot be identified; the set at best supports attribution among parallel drivers, not a clean interventional estimate. Confounder quality is therefore zero.
